key_insight: Training GPT-style models on synthetic limit order book streams reveals they learn amortized Bayesian filtering of latent market regimes rather than just surface patterns.
engineering_relevance: This suggests foundation models can become fast, low-cost surrogate inferencers for market microstructure simulators and parameter calibration workflows.
method: Train autoregressive transformers on order-flow sequences from simulators with known latent parameters
Compare next-token predictions to exact Bayes-optimal and oracle predictors under stationary and drifting regimes
Probe frozen activations to decode latent regime and test zero-shot transfer to real NASDAQ data
evidence_signal: The model’s predictive loss matches the exact Bayes optimum to within a millinat per token, and latent regime decoding outperforms baselines while transfer improves as the simulator prior better covers real flow.
watch_item: Results depend strongly on simulator coverage, so a narrow or misspecified synthetic prior may limit transfer to real markets.
paper_title: What Do Foundation Models for Market Microstructure Learn? A Controlled Study with Synthetic Limit Order Books
